label: 2026-09-06 manual-worker insanity point
population_semantics: manual runs are assigned by started_at; archive time never moves an old-format run across the boundary; post-change sanity evidence accumulates from the fixed boundary until this baseline is explicitly superseded

score_semantics.component_formula: weight * clamp((baseline-current)/baseline, -1, 1); all scored components are lower-is-better
score_semantics.important: diagnostic trend only; mixed manual-task duration is not part of the headline. Go/continue duration is a separate continuation projection. Never a worker target, completion gate, scheduler input, product acceptance signal, or run-length incentive.
score_semantics.headline_formula: min(friction_delta, operational_lifecycle_delta); continuation run duration is separate and never folded into this score

guardrails: General manual sanity scores reporting friction and lifecycle mistakes only; mixed task duration is not scored or used as a verdict guardrail.
Continuation/go duration and fragmentation are reported separately from bounded manual task durations; never use the mixed manual population to answer whether `go` runs are too short.
Do not claim continuation improvement before the continuation sample gate is met.
The score measures manual-reporting/process behavior, not model intelligence, user wellbeing, product quality, or MCP health.

friction.semantics: Measures reporting overhead directly changed by PR #658; useful as friction evidence but insufficient by itself to claim sanity improved.

operational.semantics: Measures report/execution lifecycle mistakes across actual manual execution runs. Run duration/fragmentation is intentionally excluded and tracked only for continuation go/continue runs.

continuation_baseline.source_semantics: Six hours before PR #658, using only historical manual reports explicitly identifiable as go/continue from run_id or scope; bounded historical subset, not all manual work.
continuation_baseline.important: Separate from the general manual sanity score. Do not infer go/continue quality from bounded one-shot task or correction durations; user-interrupted continuation runs should be identified by stop_reason when available.
